verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy issues virtual keys that can be restricted per key: model access, MCP tool access, spend budgets, and key-scoped guardrails. This lets a user mint a constrained credential for an agent. A community user reported trouble creating tokens for other users, which lowers confidence but is not concrete enough to dispute the documented capability. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained permission scopes beyond model/MCP access, per-key rate limits (the rpm_limit evidence is team-level), agent-specific least-privilege guidance, and independent hands-on corroboration of scoped key issuance.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Track Spend, and control model access via virtual keys for the proxy
